title: NVDLA (nvdla/hw)
_note: nvdla/hw master = the nv_full configuration as shipped in vmod/ (the
template-generated Verilog is checked in, so no tmake step).  vmod/nvdla is
(DW_minmax, DW_lsd) library, vmod/rams/model the behavioural RAM models;
vmod/rams/synth defines the same nv_ram_* names as synthesis models and is
left out so each RAM has one definition.
The gate / flop / RAM libraries NVDLA instantiates -- vmod/vlibs (the
`nv_assert_no_x` assertion wrappers and the GTECH-style cells) and
vmod/rams (the nv_ram_rws_* wrappers and their behavioural models) -- are
always_srcs, not roots: every design module needs them to elaborate (107
rows read-failed on "no definition for nv_assert_no_x" without them) but
they are library cells, not rows to sweep.
Excluded `^vmw_`: the flop-RAM wrappers NVDLA declares under `ifdef EMU`
(emulation only, 39 of them).  They appear in the module list because the
harness reads the source text, but no definition of them is elaborated.
First local survey 2026-10-26 (914 rows after that exclusion): 907 read with
0 undriven.  The 7 that do not: the whole-accelerator rows NV_nvdla,
NV_NVDLA_partition_a / _o, NV_NVDLA_cacc, NV_NVDLA_cbuf and
NV_NVDLA_CACC_assembly_buffer, which run past the row budget (the assembly
buffer alone spends 900 s expanding its 32x288 RAM banks into per-bit
latches) -- the same whole-core class as BlackParrot -- and NV_NVDLA_ssync3d,
which instantiates `p_STRICTSYNC3DOTM`, a synchroniser cell no file in the repository defines.
WHY THERE IS NO ORACLE, exactly -- and the dead end not to retry.
`read_slang` stops on `use of undeclared identifier 'assertion_error'` in
vmod/vlibs/nv_assert_{fifo,hold_throughout_event_interval,vld_credit_max}.vlib.
`assertion_error` is a TASK that vlibs declare by `include "assertion_task.h"`
INSIDE an `ifndef SYNTHESIS` block -- and in nv_assert_always.vlib the CALL is
inside that same block, so -DSYNTHESIS removes both and the file is consistent.
In those three (and nv_assert_vld_credit_max) the call is NOT under SYNTHESIS:
its only guards are `ifndef EMU` and the ELSE of `ifdef FV_ASSERT_ON`, so a
synthesis build keeps the CALL and drops the DECLARATION.  That is an upstream
packaging inconsistency, not a frontend limitation: Surelog tolerates the
undeclared task call (read_uhdm reads all 914 rows), slang does not, and
because the file is in every row's closure ALL 914 lose their reference.
DEAD END, measured 2026-10-27: adding -DFV_ASSERT_ON takes the other branch
and does skip the task call -- and then every vlib fails on
`'common_sva_assert.sva': No such file or directory`, because that include is
referenced by the FV branch of nv_assert_{always,one_hot,zero_one_hot,no_x}
and IS NOT SHIPPED anywhere in the repository.  The FV branch was never
packaged; do not reach for that define again.
The route that should work is a HARNESS STAND-IN for those four .vlib files,
the mechanism openpiton uses for its flop library: put the call under
`ifndef SYNTHESIS` exactly as nv_assert_always.vlib already does, keep the
originals in exclude_srcs, and the change is additive and reviewable.  That
would give all 914 rows a read_slang reference and finally adjudicate the 70
co-simulated divergences.
RE-SWEPT 2026-10-28 with the stand-ins (#1360), and the family now has a
formal column for the first time:
no read_slang reference    914  ->  3
formally proven              0  ->  775 / 911
elaborate                  907  ->  834 / 911
co-sim PASS                  -  ->  815
rows with 0 undriven       907  ->  907
The 70 unadjudicated divergences are adjudicated: 41 remain and they are
slang-CLEAN, i.e. genuine reader leads, which is what the oracle was for.
36 rows are `differs`.  Three rows still have no reference and all three are
slang-side, not packaging: NV_NVDLA_CACC_CALC_fp_48b exhausts slang's unroll
limit of 4000, NV_NVDLA_CACC_calculator trips an internal slang assert.
NEW and worth knowing: 75 rows now report `error` where before they were
simply not comparable -- every one of them is
`No SAT model available for cell ...r_nv_ram_rws...`, i.e. the MITER cannot
run because satgen has no model for NVDLA's RAM cell.  That is not a
regression; those rows had no miter at all before.  They need the
`tribuf -formal` / memory-mapping treatment the caliptra spi_host row got,
or the RAM behind a blackbox.
Only TWO rows now fail to elaborate (NV_nvdla and NV_NVDLA_partition_o, both
whole-accelerator, Surelog std::bad_alloc under the 7 GB cap) -- down from
the 7 of the first survey.

NV_NVDLA_BDMA_STORE_lat_fifo.note: adjudicated 2026-10-30: not a reader defect. read_slang reads this module but its netlist will not lower for Verilator, so the row has no reference. Co-simulated against the GOLDEN read_verilog netlist instead (netlist_cosim.py --slang-il, the OpenC910 / OpenPiton method): both netlists diverge from the RTL by the SAME count, 4 of 301 cycles -- an uninitialised RAM read, which each synthesis netlist resolves its own way while the behavioural model does not. All 28 of these rows that have an oracle match it EXACTLY after the level-sensitive dynamic element-write fix; before it they diverged wider than the oracle, which is what pointed at the defect.
